name: World Capitals
description: Match countries on every continent to their capital cities.
question: What is the capital of {prompt}?

cards.fact: Paris earned the nickname "City of Light" as an early adopter of gas street lighting and a hub of the Enlightenment.
London was founded by the Romans almost 2,000 years ago as Londinium.
Bonn served as West Germany's capital; Berlin became the capital of reunified Germany in 1990.
Rome completely surrounds another country: Vatican City, the smallest state in the world.
Madrid sits almost exactly in the geographic center of Spain.
A huge earthquake and tsunami destroyed much of Lisbon in 1755.
Saint Petersburg was Russia's capital for about two centuries before Moscow regained the title in 1918.
Athens is named after Athena, goddess of wisdom, whose temple the Parthenon still crowns the Acropolis.
Dublin's name comes from the Irish "Dubh Linn," meaning "black pool."
Amsterdam is the constitutional capital, but the government and parliament sit in The Hague.
Warsaw's Old Town was almost totally destroyed in WWII and rebuilt so faithfully it became a UNESCO site.
Mozart, Beethoven, Haydn and Schubert all lived and worked in Vienna.
Budapest was formed in 1873 by merging the cities of Buda, Óbuda and Pest across the Danube.
Prague is nicknamed the "City of a Hundred Spires."
Stockholm is spread across 14 islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea.
Oslo was called Christiania (later Kristiania) until 1925.
Helsinki replaced Turku as Finland's capital in 1812, under Russian rule.
Switzerland has no official capital by law; Bern is formally the "federal city" where government sits.
Reykjavík is the northernmost capital of a sovereign state.
Kyiv's Saint Sophia Cathedral dates back to the 11th century.
Bucharest's Palace of the Parliament is one of the largest administrative buildings in the world.
Sofia takes its name from the ancient Saint Sofia Church, not from a person.
Tallinn's medieval Old Town is one of the best-preserved Hanseatic towns in Europe.
Ljubljana's symbol is a dragon, which guards the city's famous Dragon Bridge.
Bratislava is the only national capital that borders two other countries: Austria and Hungary.
Valletta, built by the Knights of St. John, is the smallest capital city in the European Union.
Tokyo was called Edo until 1868, when the emperor moved there from Kyoto.
Beijing literally means "northern capital."
New Delhi was inaugurated as the capital of British India in 1931.
About half of South Korea's population lives in the Seoul metropolitan area.
Locals call Bangkok "Krung Thep," short for one of the longest city names in the world.
Hà Nội means roughly "inside the rivers," after its spot on the Red River.
Indonesia is building a new capital, Nusantara, on the island of Borneo to relieve sinking Jakarta.
The City of Manila is among the most densely populated cities on Earth.
Kuala Lumpur means "muddy confluence"; many government offices have moved to nearby Putrajaya.
Islamabad was purpose-built in the 1960s to replace Karachi as the capital.
Atatürk made Ankara the capital in 1923 instead of Istanbul, the former Ottoman seat.
Riyadh's name comes from the Arabic word for "gardens."
Tehran sits at the foot of the snowy Alborz mountains.
Dubai is the UAE's biggest city, but Abu Dhabi is the capital and largest emirate.
The Kathmandu Valley has seven UNESCO World Heritage monument zones.
Ulaanbaatar, meaning "Red Hero," is often called the coldest national capital in the world.
Astana replaced Almaty as capital in 1997, was renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019, then Astana again in 2022.
Myanmar moved its capital from Yangon to the newly built Naypyidaw in 2005–2006.
Thimphu famously has no traffic lights; police direct traffic by hand.
Cairo sits on the Nile, a short drive from the Pyramids of Giza.
Abuja officially replaced Lagos as Nigeria's capital in 1991.
Nairobi's name comes from a Maasai phrase meaning "cool water."
Addis Ababa means "new flower" in Amharic and hosts the African Union's headquarters.
Casablanca is Morocco's largest city, but the capital is coastal Rabat.
In 1957 Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African colony to win independence.
Dakar is the westernmost city on the African mainland.
Algiers is nicknamed "the White City" for its gleaming whitewashed buildings.
Antananarivo means "city of the thousand," said to honor a thousand warriors who guarded it.
Harare was called Salisbury until 1982.
Ouagadougou hosts FESPACO, the largest film festival in Africa.
Gaborone was built almost from scratch to be the capital when Botswana became independent in 1966.
Kigali is known for its cleanliness, helped by a monthly national community clean-up day, Umuganda.
Windhoek sits on a high plateau in the middle of Namibia, between two deserts: the Namib and the Kalahari.
D.C. stands for District of Columbia, a federal district that belongs to no state.
Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as the capital in 1857, partly as a compromise between rival cities.
Mexico City is built on the ruins of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, which stood on a lake.
Brasília was built from scratch and inaugurated in 1960, with buildings by Oscar Niemeyer.
Buenos Aires means "good airs" or "fair winds" in Spanish.
Santiago was founded in 1541 by the Spanish conquistador Pedro de Valdivia.
Francisco Pizarro founded Lima in 1535 as the "City of Kings."
Bogotá sits about 2,600 meters (8,500 ft) up in the Andes.
Montevideo hosted the very first FIFA World Cup final in 1930.
Asunción, founded in 1537, is one of the oldest cities in South America.
Havana's streets are famous for classic 1950s American cars still in daily use.
Bob Marley's former home in Kingston is now a museum.
Tegucigalpa's old Toncontín airport is famous for one of the trickiest landing approaches anywhere.
Belmopan became capital in 1970 after Hurricane Hattie devastated coastal Belize City in 1961.
Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise because Sydney and Melbourne both wanted to be capital.
Wellington is the southernmost capital of a sovereign state, and famously windy.
Suva is on Viti Levu, the largest of Fiji's roughly 330 islands.
Papua New Guinea has over 800 living languages, more than any other country.
